subject: dynamic occupancy using colext() for large data set - running out of memory and time

messages.subject: dynamic occupancy using colext() for large data set - running out of memory and time
parts:
Hi,

 

My question is related to dynamic occupancy using the colext() function in “unmarked”. 

 

Briefly, I am trying to estimate species richness patterns over space and time, using long-term avian point count data collected over a 12-year period. Because replicate surveys were not conducted over periods of time where closure could be assumed, I am using a space-for-time replacement approach where points are grouped based on their locations within a 750m x 750m grid framework such that each survey is a primary sampling period and the points within each grid cell are my secondary sampling occasions. Not all points were surveyed during each survey so those that were not surveyed are simply NAs (11 is the maximum number of points within a grid cell, so this is the number of secondary survey periods). The data are structured such that each row corresponds to a specific species and grid cell and each column corresponds to a specific point (~secondary sampling period) and survey (~primary sampling period).  Site level covariates are just the grid cell IDs at this point, but later I will include other habitat covariates.

One issue that I am having is that any model including even a single covariate (e.g., allowing det prob to change with year and season) is using over 25G of memory and requiring more than 4 days time – such that I am not able to run the model with the computational resources that I have available.

 

I am wondering if anyone has run into a similar issue or has any ideas as to how to deal with this problem. Any thoughts would be greatly appreciated.


Thanks!

Elise

messages.author: 4a635fe980c8c1cd
messages.subject: dynamic occupancy using colext() for large data set - running out of memory and time
parts:
I don’t know if colext has an argument for engine (I.e,
engine = ‘C’) or if it does, whether c (and not r) is the default, but calling a different engine under the unmarked hood might be the easiest way to speed things up. The only other specific unmarked option I can think of is to choose starting values carefully so that the optimizer finds
the peak in the likelihood more quickly. Maybe setting
se = FALSE saves a little time?

Otherwise, more general options (faster computers, parallel fitting, or hard-coding it in a faster language)
might be the way to go. I think Olivier Gimenez shared some code to fit a dynamic occupancy model w/ Template model builder—if I can find it, I’ll pass along (very fast, but you do need to write the likelihood out explicitly and follow c++ syntax.


W/ RAM, I don’t know. 6 million observations
is quite a bit—w/ covariates, the model matrix could get pretty large very quickly—I don’t know of a way to make these things more compact. I guess you could subsample or use a cv approach to model selection?

John
